decision: held: per Dr. Pham's fifth ruling set, the retracted-trial analysis is finished and the surviving outcomes do not meet the credit rules. Rezk 2016 (PMID 26037728, retraction 37466255) is only in the haemoglobin pool (Figure 4, 14.9% weight; 11.80 g/L in Results and the forest plot, misprinted as g/dL in the abstract), which is not accepted. The serum iron (WMD 41.44 ug/dL, 7 rows) and ferritin (WMD 13.6 ng/mL, 6 rows) pools do not contain Rezk and survive as printed. They still fail the credit rules: 3 of their rows are non-randomized (Paesano 2014; Lepanto 2018 x2; Table S1), no lactoferrin dose or form is reported anywhere in the source including Table S1, the comparator is ferrous sulfate (active, not placebo), the outcomes are iron-status surrogates, and the only double-blind RCT (Nappi 2009) is null. Exact remaining item for Dr. Pham: context ingr_lactoferrin_35276902_exact_source; lactoferrin vs ferrous sulfate in women with ID/IDA, mostly pregnant; serum iron/ferritin superiority from mixed randomized and non-randomized rows with no reported dose. Proposed conclusion: no credit for the record's assessed use (it declares no health-goal claim; labels usually claim immune support). Lactoferrin nutrition and safety stay separate.
summary: 19639462 abstract: 100 pregnant women with iron-deficiency anaemia, bovine lactoferrin 100 mg twice daily vs ferrous sulfate, with comparable haematological improvement and fewer gastrointestinal effects; this is an active-comparator iron-status finding, not immune evidence. 35276902 (Nutrients 2022) is open access, but its retracted-input hold governs; the existing pending context is left unchanged. The record declares no health-goal claim and stays held.

population.description: 11 studies from 8 articles (9 randomized, 2 non-randomized); 8 in people with iron deficiency or iron-deficiency anaemia; 6 in pregnant and 4 in non-pregnant women (some with hereditary thrombophilia); 680 lactoferrin vs 582 ferrous sulfate participants (Results).

study_contexts.study_design: Systematic review and random-effects meta-analysis of lactoferrin versus ferrous sulfate (active comparator, no placebo); primary outcomes serum iron, serum ferritin and haemoglobin.

outcomes.name: Serum iron vs ferrous sulfate: WMD 41.44 ug/dL (95% CI 26.29-56.59), 7 study rows in Figure 2 (text says 8), I2 98%; Rezk 2016 not in this pool; Nappi 2009 row null (-0.85)
Serum ferritin: WMD 13.6 ng/mL (4.53-22.66), 6 rows (Figure 3), I2 99%; Rezk not in this pool; Nappi row null (0.40)

Haemoglobin: WMD 11.80 g/L (8.19-15.41), I2 96% (Results and Figure 4, units g/L; the abstract misprints 11.80 g/dL); Figure 4 has 8 rows (text says 9) and includes the retracted Rezk 2016 trial (PMID 26037728; MD 11.50 g/L, weight 14.9%); not accepted as a pooled inference
Fractional iron absorption lower with lactoferrin (WMD -2.08%); IL-6 lower (WMD -45.59 pg/mL)

limitations: Haemoglobin unit discrepancy recorded: Results text and Figure 4 report 11.80 g/L; the abstract prints 11.80 g/dL (a tenfold error). The full-text/forest-plot basis (g/L) is used.

Retracted included trial: Rezk et al. 2016 (PMID 26037728; retraction notice 37466255) contributes only to the haemoglobin pool (Figure 4, 14.9% weight). Serum iron (Figure 2) and ferritin (Figure 3) pools do not include it and are reported as printed. The haemoglobin estimate is not recomputed here and is not accepted.
Study counts differ between text and forest plots (serum iron 8 vs 7 rows; haemoglobin 9 vs 8 rows); retained, not resolved.

Active-comparator (ferrous sulfate) surrogate outcomes in iron deficiency, mostly pregnancy; most pooled rows are from the Paesano/Lepanto groups with unclear or high risk-of-bias items; not immune or general-wellness evidence.
Context authored and source-verified by agent review (Claude) on 2026-10-28; Dr. Pham's pre-approval of fully source-verified contexts attested by Sean on 2026-10-28.

Supplementary Table S1 (retrieved 2026-10-28 from the Europe PMC supplementary files) lists intervention only as 'lactoferrin; ferrous sulfate' with duration (28 days to 8 weeks, or until delivery) and gives no lactoferrin dose, form or iron content; dose is recorded as not reported by the source.

Surviving pools without Rezk: serum iron (Figure 2, 7 rows: Lepanto 2018 x2, Nappi 2009, Paesano 2006/2010-1/2010-2/2014) and ferritin (Figure 3, 6 rows) do not contain Rezk 2016, so their printed conclusions are unaffected by the retraction. However, Table S1 marks Paesano 2014 and both Lepanto 2018 cohorts as non-randomized (populations with hereditary thrombophilia), these carry high/unclear risk-of-bias items, most rows come from one research group, and the one double-blind RCT (Nappi 2009) is null on serum iron (-0.85) and ferritin (0.40). The pools are therefore not meta-analyses of RCTs only and do not meet the credit rules.
